grades.quote: FENCE.I does _not_ ensure that other RISC-V harts' instruction fetches will observe the local hart’s stores in a multiprocessor system. To make a store to instruction memory visible to all RISC-V harts, the writing hart also has to execute a data FENCE before requesting that all remote RISC-V harts execute a FENCE.I.
grades.reason: Directly answers: FENCE.I only ensures the local hart's subsequent instruction fetches see its prior stores; it does not ensure other harts' fetches observe them, so remote harts must also execute FENCE.I after a data FENCE.
Discusses SFENCE.VMA and ASIDs/address-translation caches, not FENCE.I or instruction-fetch synchronization across harts.
Alloy formalization of FENCE preserved program order for data memory operations; does not address FENCE.I or instruction fetch synchronization across harts.

grades.quote: SFENCE.VMA orders only the local hart’s implicit references to the memory-management data structures.
grades.reason: Concerns SFENCE.VMA, not FENCE.I, but shows an analogous local-only fence scope and the need to notify other harts. It is only tangentially related to the instruction-fetch question.
